The tests pass: 7 passed, exit code 0. That covers the four earlier tests plus the three new ones for keeping language, keeping unknown keys, and not modifying the input.

What `reset(prefs)` in prefs.py now does:
- It sets theme, font_size, autosave_minutes and show_line_numbers back to their defaults.
- It keeps whatever `language` the user picked. If there is no language in the input, it falls back to the default `en`.
- It keeps any unknown keys as they are.
- It does not modify the dict you pass in.

The tests are ones I wrote, so they show the function does what I intended, not that it matches how the app behaves. Please look at the `PRESERVED_ON_RESET` constant and the `reset` body yourself. To protect another setting from reset later, add it to that tuple.

The reset button still does nothing, because the settings screen is in the desktop version, which isn't in this workspace. Nobody has tested the button end to end. Whoever owns the desktop code needs to make the handler call `prefs.reset(current_prefs)` and then `prefs.save(path, result)`. If you find that project, point me at it and I can look at the wiring.

The only files changed are prefs.py and tests/test_prefs.py, and nothing was deleted. I recorded your two decisions and the UI-wiring gap as notes. The notes from before your answers, which still list those two questions as open, are now out of date.

diff --git a/prefs.py b/prefs.py
index ea1caf8..6409ed6 100644
--- a/prefs.py
+++ b/prefs.py
@@ -9,6 +9,9 @@ DEFAULTS = {
     "show_line_numbers": False,
 }
 
+# Keys that 'Reset to defaults' leaves as the user set them.
+PRESERVED_ON_RESET = ("language",)
+
 
 def load(path):
     """Saved preferences laid over the defaults."""
@@ -26,5 +29,16 @@ def save(path, prefs):
 
 
 def reset(prefs):
-    """Preferences after the user presses 'Reset to defaults'."""
-    raise NotImplementedError
+    """Preferences after the user presses 'Reset to defaults'.
+
+    Appearance and behaviour settings go back to DEFAULTS. Keys in
+    PRESERVED_ON_RESET (language) and any unknown keys are kept as they are.
+    The dict passed in is not modified.
+    """
+    result = dict(prefs)
+    for key, value in DEFAULTS.items():
+        if key in PRESERVED_ON_RESET:
+            result.setdefault(key, value)
+        else:
+            result[key] = value
+    return result
diff --git a/tests/test_prefs.py b/tests/test_prefs.py
index 574c92e..0e43561 100644
--- a/tests/test_prefs.py
+++ b/tests/test_prefs.py
@@ -11,3 +11,35 @@ def test_save_and_load_keeps_changes(tmp_path):
     loaded = prefs.load(p)
     assert loaded["theme"] == "dark"
     assert loaded["font_size"] == prefs.DEFAULTS["font_size"]
+
+
+def test_reset_restores_defaults():
+    changed = {**prefs.DEFAULTS, "theme": "dark", "font_size": 20}
+    assert prefs.reset(changed) == prefs.DEFAULTS
+
+
+def test_reset_returns_copy_not_defaults_itself():
+    result = prefs.reset({})
+    result["theme"] = "dark"
+    assert prefs.DEFAULTS["theme"] == "light"
+
+
+def test_reset_keeps_language():
+    changed = {**prefs.DEFAULTS, "language": "es", "theme": "dark"}
+    result = prefs.reset(changed)
+    assert result["language"] == "es"
+    assert result["theme"] == prefs.DEFAULTS["theme"]
+
+
+def test_reset_keeps_unknown_keys():
+    changed = {**prefs.DEFAULTS, "font_size": 20, "future_option": [1, 2]}
+    result = prefs.reset(changed)
+    assert result["future_option"] == [1, 2]
+    assert result["font_size"] == prefs.DEFAULTS["font_size"]
+
+
+def test_reset_does_not_modify_input():
+    changed = {"theme": "dark", "language": "es", "extra": 1}
+    snapshot = dict(changed)
+    prefs.reset(changed)
+    assert changed == snapshot
